{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv')

# Filter out QA orders, refunded orders, and missing age
valid_df = df[~(df['revenue'] == '999999.99')]
valid_df = valid_df[valid_df['status'] == 'completed']
valid_df = valid_df[valid_df['customer_age'] != -1]

# Convert revenue to float
valid_df['revenue'] = valid_df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Now compute conversion rates by channel and customer_segment
conversion_by_channel_segment = valid_df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().unstack(level='customer_segment')
print('Conversion rates by channel and customer segment:')
print(conversion_by_channel_segment)

# Compute the overall difference (email - paid_search) in conversion rates
# But note: this is still confounded by segment
email_rate = valid_df[valid_df['channel'] == 'email']['converted'].mean()
paid_search_rate = valid_df[valid_df['channel'] == 'paid_search']['converted'].mean()
difference = email_rate - paid_search_rate

# Also compute the weighted average difference by segment to show the confounding
# We'll compute the difference within each segment
n_email = valid_df[valid_df['channel'] == 'email'].groupby('customer_segment').size()
n_paid_search = valid_df[valid_df['channel'] == 'paid_search'].groupby('customer_segment').size()

# Compute within-segment differences
within_segment_diff = []
for seg in ['new', 'returning', 'loyal']:
    email_seg = valid_df[(valid_df['channel'] == 'email') & (valid_df['customer_segment'] == seg)]['converted'].mean()
    paid_search_seg = valid_df[(valid_df['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (valid_df['customer_segment'] == seg)]['converted'].mean()
    diff = email_seg - paid_search_seg
    within_segment_diff.append((seg, email_seg, paid_search_seg, diff))

print('\nWithin-segment differences:')
for seg, email, paid, diff in within_segment_diff:
    print(f'{seg}: email={email:.4f}, paid_search={paid:.4f}, difference={diff:.4f}')"}
